findings.title: Async forEach is fire-and-forget, calendar/video deletions never awaited
findings.body: In packages/app-store/vital/lib/reschedule.ts line 125 bookingRefsFiltered.forEach(async (bookingRef) => ...) creates async callbacks whose promises are never awaited or returned. The surrounding try/catch cannot catch rejections from them, Reschedule returns true before deleteEvent/deleteMeeting finish, and failures are silently lost leaving orphaned calendar/video events.

findings.title: Async forEach is fire-and-forget, calendar/video deletions never awaited
findings.body: In packages/app-store/wipemycalother/lib/reschedule.ts line 125 bookingRefsFiltered.forEach(async (bookingRef) => ...) is not awaited. The async deleteEvent/deleteMeeting calls run detached, errors bypass the try/catch, and the function can return before cleanup completes, leaving stale external events.

findings.title: Async forEach for bookingRef deletion never awaited
findings.body: In packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings.tsx line 553 bookingRefsFiltered.forEach(async (bookingRef) => ...) fires calendar?.deleteEvent and deleteMeeting without collecting the promises. The requestReschedule mutation then sends reschedule email and webhooks without waiting for external cancellations, and any rejection is unhandled.

findings.title: Async forEach pushes to apiDeletes after it is consumed
findings.body: In packages/features/bookings/lib/handleCancelBooking.ts around line 460 bookingToDelete.user.credentials.filter(...).forEach(async (credential) => ...) awaits getCalendar then pushes to apiDeletes inside the async callback. The outer forEach is not awaited, so the later await Promise.all(prismaPromises.concat(apiDeletes)) at line 652 can run before pushes happen. Recurring-booking cancellations can therefore skip deleting external calendar events entirely and never surface errors.

findings.title: Dynamic imports are eager, defeating lazy-loading intent
findings.body: In packages/app-store/index.ts the object literal applecalendar: import("./applecalendar"), etc. executes every import() as soon as the module is evaluated, starting ~30 parallel chunk loads on every server boot/request path that imports appStore. Callers still await appStore[key], so correctness is preserved, but there is no on-demand loading. Use getters or functions returning import() to make loading truly lazy.

findings.title: Unvalidated credential type can throw and unhandled import rejection
findings.body: In packages/app-store/_utils/getCalendar.ts line 15 calendarType.split("_").join("") assumes calendarType is a non-empty string and that the key exists in appStore. If credential.type is null/undefined or an unknown app, .split throws TypeError, and if the dynamic import() rejects (missing chunk) the rejection propagates to all callers. Previously a sync lookup returned undefined and logged a warning. Add a guard for missing type/unknown key and catch import failure to return null.
